cells.tense: The ending is happening at the right time, and it is being done cleanly.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Where you'd normally hand back exactly what you were handed, receive one kindness without settling it, and pass one along without watching for the return. No ledger, no deadline.
cells.core:
An ending is underway in your life and you're doing it well. You can feel when something has finished — not by argument, by a sense of what can't go on — and you've let it end without dragging out a farewell or turning it into a fight. What's coming next isn't clear, and you're fine with the fog. When a step shows itself you take it, and the taken steps have been landing true.

The fairness you keep in all this is part of why it holds. Where you've been living by handing back exactly what you're handed, be a little looser. Take one kindness without counting it and return one without waiting to be repaid, so the exchange moves in both directions without you holding it. It keeps the new thing fed while the shape of it is still forming.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is yours, and you're doing it clean.
cells.verb: ending what's finished, so the new thing has room
cells.place: in thick fog where each step is lit only as you take it

cells.tense: You will keep being the one who clears the room, and the clearing keeps outrunning the life.
cells.act: feel it alongside them and keep your own side
cells.ask: When the urge to end something arrives, don't act on it that day. Stay beside whoever it touches and let what they carry reach you, without agreeing with them or taking their position as your own.
cells.core:
The clearing has picked up speed. Things get ended here before they've had a life — a plan, a situation, a way of working — and each ending gets called freedom, though it arrives right before you'd have to try. You're braced a season ahead, shutting things down so they can't disappoint you first. The fog isn't the trouble; you're moving too fast for it to matter what's actually there.

What's missing is someone else's reality next to yours. Before the next ending, sit with whoever it touches and feel how it looks from where they sit, without merging into it or talking them out of it. You can leave after. The difference is whether you left knowing what you left.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing has outrun the life it was clearing.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that closed behind you, and you are still standing there.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Notice which direction something in you keeps tugging toward, and follow it once — a call, a place, an hour spent on it — before you've worked out whether it's sensible.
cells.core:
Something in your life has already ended and you're treating it as ongoing. You keep the routines, the care, the showing up, long after whatever it was stopped being alive, and calling that loyalty is the kindest name for it. The fog has been an excuse here — no clear path, so none taken — and still days pass in which nothing moves toward anything you'd choose.

Nothing gets cleared by waiting. Notice which way something in you is already leaning, and follow that lean once, before you've decided it's sensible or found the whole route. The fog doesn't lift first; the step is what lights the next stretch. What you're keeping doesn't need another month of you. What's next does need the step.
cells.sheetLine: You keep a thing that's finished. It doesn't keep you.
cells.verb: ending what's finished, so the new thing has room
cells.place: in thick fog where each step is lit only as you take it

cells.tense: Something has been ending here, and you are still writing as if it has not.
cells.act: write the order things go in
cells.ask: Take one page and set down the order your days actually run in — what comes first, what follows, what you'd keep if you had to choose. Written plainly, no verdict on any of it.
cells.core:
An ending is underway in your life and it hasn't reached your account of things. You keep planning on ground that is quietly shifting, and someone who asks how it's going gets the version from before. The fog gets blamed for the uncertainty, but the uncertainty sits downstream of something you haven't put a word to yet. That's all that's missing — a word, not the ending.

Give what's here a container. One page holding the order your days actually run in — what comes first, what follows, what you'd keep if the choice were forced — so the shape is written down rather than carried silently. You don't have to decide anything from it. Once it's on the page, what has been ending usually says so.

attempts.check: The one thing the record doesn't support is any claim about what is actually ending in this person's life — the draw names necessary endings and clearing, but nothing says what those are, how long they've been running, or who is involved, so the cells locate the capacity and its bend, never the content. A reader could reasonably say that imagining endings and living one aren't the same, and that the seat reading sounds like second-guessing rather than a strength; the asks still hold because each is a small act of the partner, doable in a week regardless of what the ending turns out to be. The sentence that serves me more than the person is the balanced core's 'trust the path that reveals itself' — it sounds knowing without giving them anywhere to put their hands, so the core turns it into something done.
